extracted.intended_audience: K-12 mathematics teachers and curriculum leaders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for teaching K–12 mathematics that develop students' mathematical habits of mind (problem solving, reasoning, representation, communication, and use of tools) aligned to TX TEKS, CCSS, and NCTM process standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: College and Career Readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is every student graduating from high school ready for success in college or a well-paying career?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References common assessments/standards (ACT, The College Board, CCSS, Texas CCRS) as frameworks for expectations about students' readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: TX College & Career Readiness: desired dispositions and skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should develop intellectual curiosity, reasoning, problem solving, academic behaviors, work habits, academic integrity, reading/writing/research across the curriculum, use of data, and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dispositions and skills are listed as part of the Texas College & Career Readiness Standards and underpin readiness for postsecondary success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop ways of thinking about mathematics (CCRS principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must develop ways of thinking about mathematics; these key cognitive skills elevate mathematics from rote memorization to a process of analysis and interpretation enabling learners to work with complex questions, topics, and issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical thinking should be embedded in appropriate content rather than taught in isolation (quote from CCRS, p. 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a 'Doer' of Mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Students learn mathematics by doing mathematics — active engagement in mathematical work is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Paul Halmos) Emphasizes experiential/problem-based learning rather than passive reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thinking like a Mathematician
rubrics_metrics.description: Doing mathematics (figuring out hard problems); reasoning, explaining, and arguing; zooming in and zooming out; exploration that is sometimes messy; trying things that sometimes work and sometimes don't; reflecting, considering, analyzing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These behaviors describe the cognitive habits educators should nurture to help students think mathematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Big Three: understanding, doing, using math
rubrics_metrics.description: All students need: understanding math (making sense), doing math (skills, facts, procedures), and using math (thinking, reasoning, applying, solving a range of problems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should balance conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application/problem solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: The New Basics: deep transferable skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem solving, reasoning, research, communication, creativity are essential transferable skills for students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 'new basics' support versatilizing students' mathematical knowledge across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Habits of Mind (general list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performing thought experiments; finding, articulating, and explaining patterns; creating and using representations; generalizing from examples; articulating generality in precise language; expecting mathematics to make sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Al Cuoco, Goldenberg, Mark — these are cognitive tools/strategies that serve as 'connective tissue' for mathematical content and should be infused in instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCTM Process Standard: Problem Solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem Solving as a core process standard (NCTM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage students to formulate, tackle, and learn from problems; appears as one of NCTM's five process standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCTM Process Standard: Reasoning and Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasoning and Proof as a core process standard (NCTM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should develop skills in making and critiquing mathematical arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCTM Process Standard: Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication as a core process standard (NCTM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should explain mathematical thinking orally and in writing; communication supports learning and justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCTM Process Standard: Connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Connections as a core process standard (NCTM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should relate mathematics to other mathematical topics and to real-world contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCTM Process Standard: Representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Representations as a core process standard (NCTM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple representations (diagrams, symbols, graphs) to model and understand situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCSS Mathematical Practice 1: Make sense & persevere
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage problem interpretation, planning, sustained effort, and checking reasonableness of solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCSS Mathematical Practice 2: Reason abstractly & quantitatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason abstractly and quantitatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should contextualize and decontextualize quantities and structure within problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCSS Mathematical Practice 3: Construct arguments & critique reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct viable arguments; critique others' reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop abilities to justify conclusions and respond to others' arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCSS Mathematical Practice 4: Model with mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Model with mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mathematics to represent, analyze, and solve real-world situations; interpret results in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCSS Mathematical Practice 5: Use appropriate tools strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate tools strategically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and use tools (manipulatives, calculators, software) with understanding of their affordances and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCSS Mathematical Practice 6: Attend to precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend to precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear definitions, precise language, and careful computation; balance precision with context and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCSS Mathematical Practice 7: Look for and use structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for and make use of structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help students notice patterns and properties that simplify problems or reveal deeper relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCSS Mathematical Practice 8: Look for regularity in reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for and make use of regularity in reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage generalization from repeated reasoning and pattern recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEKS Process Standard (A): apply mathematics to real problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (References CCRS, CCSSM 1, 4; NCTM 1) Emphasizes relevance and application.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEKS Process Standard (B): problem-solving model
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (References CCRS; CCSSM 1; NCTM 1) Explicit steps for students' problem solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEKS Process Standard (C): select tools & techniques appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (References CCRS; CCSSM 1, 5; NCTM 1, 5) Emphasizes matching tool/technique to task.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEKS Process Standard (D): communicate using multiple representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (References CCRS; CCSSM 2, 3, 6; NCTM 2, 3, 5) Supports clarity and transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEKS Process Standard (E): create and use representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (References CCRS; CCSSM 3, 5; NCTM 3, 5) Use representations as thinking tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEKS Process Standard (F): analyze relationships to connect ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (References CCRS; CCSSM 3; NCTM 3, 4) Emphasizes relational thinking across topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEKS Process Standard (G): display, explain, justify with precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Display, explain, and justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (References CCRS; CCSSM 3, 6; NCTM 2) Encourages precise vocabulary and argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Solving, Applications, Mathematical Modeling (guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persevere in solving problems; explain to self; analyze givens and constraints; consider analogous problems; represent in different ways; search for regularity/trends; plan solution path; solve problems that apply the mathematics being learned; solve problems that may involve mathematics not yet learned; use mathematical modeling for ill-defined problems and interpret/reflect/fine-tune the model; zoom in/out and evaluate reasonableness of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When solving problems keep the big picture while attending to details; includes modeling as iterative and evaluative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoning, Explaining, Justifying (guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes quantitative reasoning; make sense of quantities and relationships; make conjectures and explore their truth; analyze situations and use counterexamples; justify conclusions and communicate/respond to arguments; decide whether others' arguments make sense and ask clarifying questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports development of argumentation and critical evaluation skills (linked to Process Standard G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing, Connecting, Communicating Precisely (guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for commonalities/relationships in similar problems; coherently represent a problem; decontextualize and contextualize; communicate precisely; use clear definitions and place precision in perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing precision with purpose; use precise definitions and vocabulary to reveal mathematical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools: select and understand tool limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pencil/paper, manipulatives/concrete models, compass, protractor, calculator, spreadsheet, CAS, software, internet/research, mental math; find and use external information; make decisions and understand limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach students to choose tools strategically and to be aware of tool constraints in solving problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Habits of Instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a problem-centered, upside-down teaching model; use appropriate technology appropriately; learn to zoom out, zoom in, and go back and forth; help students learn to notice and use patterns and properties within and across mathematical topics and problems; use formative assessment to pay attention to learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should infuse mathematical habits of mind rather than 'teach' them separately; formative assessment monitors thinking and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upside-down teaching model (You - We - I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shift from 'I - We - You' to 'You - We - I': start with a rich problem, students engage with the problem, discussion and comparison, teacher helps students connect and notice what they've learned, then practice and homework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start instruction with rich contextual problems to encourage student thinking before explicit instruction and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pause answer-getting; prioritize learning over speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid rushing to answers—postpone answer-getting to use problems for teaching unit mathematics; emphasize finishing only when students have learned, not when tasks are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast between instructional cultures (example: 'How can I teach my kids to get the answer?' vs 'How can I use this problem to teach the mathematics of this unit?').

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth Mindset and High Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge fixed vs malleable intelligence; teacher and student beliefs influence confidence, perseverance, and willingness to take risks; high expectations mean challenging beliefs and setting challenging standards for all students, ensuring opportunities to struggle and succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modest interventions targeting beliefs can make a difference; teachers should never assume where students will end up and must do whatever it takes for students to achieve standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing factors that limit student potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider student factors (motivation, intelligence, beliefs), teacher factors (beliefs, knowledge, expectations), instructional factors, nature of the task, opportunities to struggle and think, expectations of success, and an environment of trust/collaboration/respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design instruction and classroom climate to remove barriers and provide equitable opportunities for developing mathematical thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and formative feedback (implicit guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use formative assessment to pay attention to learning and to inform instruction that fosters mathematical habits of mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formative assessment should capture students' thinking processes (not just answers) and guide next instructional moves.
